recipes.name: Best Bread Pudding with Vanilla Sauce
ingredients_raw: 10 slices hearty farmhouse-style bread, toasted and cut into cubes

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease a 2-quart baking dish.
Make bread pudding: Whisk milk, sugar, beaten eggs, melted butter, brown sugar, and cinnamon together in a large bowl until well combined.
Gently stir in bread cubes and raisins.

Lightly spoon mixture into the prepared baking dish. Bake in the preheated oven until browned and set in the middle, 50 to 55 minutes; cover the dish with aluminum foil after 30 minutes to prevent excessive browning. Let pudding stand for 10 minutes before serving.
Meanwhile, make vanilla sauce: Whisk milk, brown sugar, egg, melted butter, flour, cinnamon, and salt together in a heavy saucepan until smooth.
Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until sauce is thickened and coats the back of a spoon, 10 to 12 minutes. Stir in vanilla.
Pour sauce over warm bread pudding or serve on the side in a bowl.

raw_recipe.headline: Best Bread Pudding with Vanilla Sauce
raw_recipe.description: My mom’s best bread pudding recipe is rich with milk and eggs and chock-full of raisins. It’s delicious served warm with a silky vanilla sauce.

video.description: In this video, you’ll see how to make a rich bread pudding with plump, juicy raisins and a creamy vanilla sauce. If you like, try this recipe with other dried fruits, like cranberries, apples, apricots, or blueberries.

review.reviewBody: Hi all, it's me, SouthernGma. Wanted to let you know that if you have leftover hamburger, hotdog buns or rolls for sub sandwiches, you can split them and toast on a tray in the oven and use up that extra bread in making this bread pudding. Works just as well and a good way to use up bread before you have to feed it to the birds or toss it. 1/2 of a burger, hotdog or sub roll will equasl one slice of farmhouse-style bread.

This is sooooo good! I just used reg white bread & altho I added 4 extra slices, I don't think it was enough because the pudding was a little too mushy for my taste. My fault tho, not the recipe's. If I use reg bread again, I think I would use at least 6 extras, possibly even more. The vanilla sauce is totally different than other vanilla sauce I've had/made before. It's thicker, like a thinned out pudding, so it kind of spreads over the bread pudding, instead of soaking down into the bread. It threw me at first but I really liked it! 1 more note, I put mine into a 3 qt dish because that's what I had availble. It baked perfectly in that size, puffing up over the top, but not spilling over & I didn't have to cover it at all, it was perfectly golden. Of course, it deflated while cooling(normal). I'm not sure mine would've fit into a 2 qt dish, as called for in the recipe.

I added nutmeg, cinnamon and raisins pre soaked in rum and wine and evaporated milk with less whole milk to the mixture and soaked it over night. I also used a special cinnamon loaf bread. Came out beautiful and very tasty.

This is a very good recipe as it stands. I'd give it a 4.9 stars. The only reason it wouldn't get the 5 stars because I feel that it is too sweet. I did make a few changes and one was to decrease the amount of sugar by about 1/2 cup. I also like apples in my bread pudding so a cut a large gala apple into small pieces and cooked it up in a little butter and sugar along with the raisins to soften them. I also put about 4 drops of lemon juice in them when i finished cooking them and let them cool. I added them to the rest of the ingredients as called for. AWESOME!
Best bread pudding ever! The one substitution that I did was to replace the whole milk with heavy cream … makes a huge difference.

I added blue berries till my heart told me enough instead of raisins. I have a blueberry bushes full of them at the moment. I used a full loaf of Wal-Mart brand italian bread, from the bakery, chopped up. I doubled the recipe because I like to share with my eldery neighbors. I used a tall 9x13 pan.

Yum! Not the healthiest dessert there ever was, but definitely comfort dessert. 

I had to loosely follow this recipe, as I was working with two 8x8 pans and trying to do it easy as possible. Greased the pans, put in my toasted banana bread pieces in each, added grated Macintosh apple to one, with a handful of dried cranberries, sprinkles of: the brown sugar only, cinnamon, nutmeg, dry grated orange peel, pieces of margarine stick cut up all over it, not trying to over sweeten it. The other pan added frozen blueberries, cinnamon, nutmeg, the other half of the brown sugar only (next time it needs more or some white sugar added), the margarine pieces, too. Then, mixed the whole milk with 4 eggs instead so in theory each would get two. I cooked it at 350 for the time it said, abs it came out perfectly like pudding should be. The sauce goes perfect with it. The apple one could use more apple in it, and I bet raisins would be fantastic with it, but cranberries because my middle child hates raisins. The blueberry one needs like tiny diced strawberries added plus some of the white sugar added, and maybe more passes of cinnamon and nutmeg. I may make this all over again, maybe with peaches or something, too. Thank you so much for posting this recipe, truly!
I made this today, in the sauce add a extra table spoon of flour. I added 1 tablespoon of rum. This was so good.

I'm in love! After reading many of the reviews, I decided to half the white sugar to 3/4 cup and it was the perfect amount of sweetness for us. We aren't crazy about raisins so I used a cup of pecans instead. I used day old Sunbeam white bread, so I took the advise of one reviewer and increased the number of slices to 16 so it wouldn't be soggy. It turned out just right. The sauce is heavenly - no changes made there. This bread pudding recipe is definitely a keeper!

Really easy and very good. I made a couple of changes -- only 1 cup of sugar in the bread pudding itself since many reviews say it is a little too sweet. and I added two diced pears because I needed to use them up. I used brioche, two cups of half-and-half and one cup of whipping cream. Just delicious. I made the sauce exactly as written, except I added some additional cinnamon. I will definitely make again.

I have been making this for years!! 6 years to be exact and even people that said they dont like bread pudding or think it is weird have loved it. I only use 1 cup of sugar instead of 1 1/2 cups because its really sweet. My family now prefers it with the lesser amount of sugar. I also take this exact recipe for the vanilla sauce and add 1/4 cup of bourbon. YUM
excellent recipe
I think I used too much bread as loaves are cut thinner and thicker - I wish there was a better way to convey the amount of bread! Therefore, it was a little dry! Vanilla Sauce was really good!
Best with no raisins and add some nutmeg
This is just the best! I lowered the sugar and added chocolate chips bc my daughter doesn’t like raisins. Delicious!
This is absolutely delicious as written. Good both warm and cold. I didn't think my sauce would come out just right, but it's perfect. Thank you for a great recipe.
Awesomely simple & tasty 😋!! This time I put 1 cup of lightly crushed blueberries to the finished sauce a min or 2 before it was almost ready. Absolute hit💯

I've never made bread pudding before but I love it. So I found this recipe made it it was so good the vanilla sauce was the bomb. Although the sauce wasn't white idk what I did wrg but was still so so so good.
I add brandy I soak raisins and walnuts overnight in brandy and then I pour it over the bread before the mixture is ready
Used exact recipe. Perfect as is. The vanilla sauce definitely takes it to the next level. Awesome!
